newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. SAYS IRAQI OIL PRICE FORMULA IS APPROVED.
newsitem.headline: U.N. SAYS IRAQI OIL PRICE FORMULA IS APPROVED.

text.p: Iraq's oil pricing formula for second round "oil-for-food" sales was formally approved Friday, after no objections were raised by U.N. Sanctions Committee members by the 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) deadline, U.N. spokesman Hiro Ueki said.
"No objections have been raised by any members of the sanctions committee," said Ueki.
Iraq is now free to submit oil contracts to U.N. overseers for renewing exports for the first time since the end of May.

U.N. overseers recommended approval of the pricing mechanism to the sanctions panel on Wednesday. Committee member states then had 48 hours to decline the price guidelines, under the so-called "no-objection" procedure.
The deadline passed Friday morning without any objections, Ueki said.
Even though the U.N. Security Council renewed the oil accord from June 8, Iraq has not lifted any oil under the plan, insisting that an aid distribution scheme be in place before starting sales.

Now, Iraq is left with little less than a month to sell up to $1 billion of the $2-billion (actually $2.14 billion including pipeline fees for Turkey) accord's limit. The terms of the deal demand Iraq export the total in two separate 90-day periods, the first ending on September 5.

More than two-thirds of the oil proceeds are earmarked for Iraq to buy food, medicine and other supplies for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed after Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in August, 1990.
